title: Introduction to AI Safety, Ethics, and Society
pitch: The Center for AI Safety's free textbook: catastrophic risks, how AI works, safety engineering, complex systems, ethics, collective action and governance in one place.

chapters.g: Why AI risk needs many fields at once, and how the book is laid out so you can read chapters in any order.
Four sources of catastrophe: malicious use, AI races, organisational risks and rogue AIs, with stories that make each concrete.
chapters.part: Section I: AI and Societal-Scale Risks

chapters.g: How modern AI works: machine learning, deep learning, scaling laws and how to think about speed of progress.
chapters.part: Section I: AI and Societal-Scale Risks

chapters.g: Problems with one AI system: monitoring, robustness, honesty, power seeking, proxy gaming and deception.
Lessons from other high risk fields: defence in depth, the Swiss cheese model, safety culture and black swans.
Why AI and society behave like complex systems, where simple fixes have surprising side effects.
What it would mean for AI to be good: wellbeing, preferences, fairness and building ethics into machines.
Game theory, races and arms dynamics: why actors who each act sensibly can produce a bad outcome together.
Options for governing AI at company, national and international levels, including compute governance.
Appendix: how utility functions work and their limits as models of what agents want.
Appendix: the main ethical theories, explained for readers new to philosophy.

ideas: AI risk is a societal problem, not only a technical one.
Catastrophic risks come from misuse, races, organisational failures and rogue AI.
Safety engineering from other industries applies to AI.
Competition can push everyone to cut corners.

args.a: A broad, many field approach is needed to understand AI risk.
args.c: Some technical researchers prefer deep focus on alignment methods over breadth.

questions: Which of the four sources of catastrophic risk seems most urgent to you?
What does the Swiss cheese model suggest for AI labs?
Can you think of a collective action problem in your college or city?

quiz.q: Which is NOT one of the book's four sources of catastrophic risk?
quiz.w: The four are malicious use, AI races, organisational risks and rogue AIs.

quiz.q: The Swiss cheese model is about...
quiz.w: Each layer has holes, but stacked layers block most failures.

quiz.q: What licence is the arXiv version under?
quiz.w: That licence lets the text be shared unchanged, non commercially, with credit.
